title: My Grandpa Left Me $1,000,000 If I Could Keep His Parrot Quiet 🦜
lines: I was standing at my grandpa's funeral when his parrot flew onto the coffin and yelled my bank password to two hundred people.
That's not my... okay, that's my password.
You see, a week earlier, my grandpa's will said I'd get one million dollars if I could keep his parrot quiet for one full day.
I signed immediately. How hard could it be to keep a bird quiet?
Well, the parrot's name was Captain. And Captain had been listening to everything in that house for forty years.
He knew every secret, every swear word, and the Wi-Fi password.
Hour one, I gave him a cracker.
He said that to me! That doesn't count!
So I covered his cage with a blanket. That's how you put birds to sleep.
He fell asleep, all right. Then he started sleep talking. In Grandpa's voice.
Don't tell my grandson about the money in the freezer.
I froze. Then I ran to the freezer.
Inside was one frozen chicken nugget and a note that said, "Nice try."
I'm not proud of it. I ate the nugget.
Hour six, I taught him sign language so he wouldn't need to talk.
He learned it in ten minutes. Then he signed something I can't repeat.
By hour twelve, I was desperate. I put headphones on him and played whale sounds.
He loved it. He started singing along. Like, professionally. My neighbor started filming.
The video got a million views. The lawyer said singing counts as words.
Starting over. Also, can I get an autograph?
Hour eighteen, I tried to bore him to sleep. I read him Grandpa's taxes.
He fell asleep in two minutes. Then he woke up and corrected my math.
So I made a plan. Final attempt. I'd sit in front of him in total silence. No TV. No phone. No crackers.
Hour twenty-three. Fifty-nine minutes. I was staring at him. He was staring at me.
Then the doorbell rang. It was my cousin Derek. Grandpa's other grandson.
Hey, Captain! Say "Derek is the best"!
Come on, buddy. Who's the favorite grandson? Say Derek!
Derek wanted the money too. He even brought crackers. The good ones.
Captain opened his beak. I couldn't breathe.
Then he closed it, flew across the room, and landed on my shoulder.
The clock hit twenty-four hours. Silence.
Derek dropped to his knees. I couldn't believe it.
Why did you stay quiet, Captain?
He leaned in and whispered in Grandpa's voice.
I wanted to cry. Every Sunday for ten years, I visited Grandpa. Derek visited once. For the Wi-Fi.
Grandpa always told me, "Anybody can talk. Not everybody listens."
Captain wasn't the test. The visits were.
Then the lawyer cleared his throat.
One more thing. You also inherit Captain.
Which brings us back to the funeral.
I changed my password. He already knows the new one.
